{{Quote|We have no search warrant. But we’re invoking act thirteen, paragraph six of the Uniform Planetary Code. We have compelling reason to believe that there is a crime in progress and lives are in danger.|Detective Sergeant Husin|<ref name="MK">''[[X-Wing: Mercy Kill]]''</ref>}}
The '''Uniform Planetary Code''' was a legal code that governed law enforcement procedures on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Kuratooine]]. Under act thirteen, paragraph six, of the code, law enforcement officers could conduct a search without a search warrant if they had compelling reason to believe that a crime was in progress and lives were in danger.<ref name="MK" />

In [[44 ABY]],<ref name="TERC">''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'' dates the events of ''[[X-Wing: Mercy Kill]]'' to [[44 ABY]].</ref> [[Police officer/Legends|police officer]] Husin and his partner [[Biller]] responded to a call by [[Kadd Yinkle]] to the [[Major Saving's Army Surplus]] store in [[Kura City]]. According to Yinkle, a [[Technician/Legends|technician]] from a security firm, they had traced the rescue transmitter of their kidnapped client, the famous pop [[Musician/Legends|singer]] [[Ledina Chott]], to the store. When they inquired at the entrance, Husin invoked the code to search the premises without a warrant when speaking to the [[Unidentified female Pop-Dog (Husin victim)|woman]] who answered his knock.<ref name="MK" />
